attacks.claim: The plan makes a proprietary, hosted-only Cirrus Cloud the sole sync backend in 5.0 and archives the stride-server Docker image. This breaks the charter/README promise of self-hosting and data ownership for ~3,000 self-hosted instances, and the MIT project would depend on a closed binary SDK with no self-hostable server.
attacks.evidence: "after which Cirrus Cloud becomes the single sync backend and the stride-server Docker image is archived"; "the server component is available only as the hosted Cirrus Cloud service"

attacks.claim: The Cirrus client SDK is a prebuilt binary under a commercial license, shipped in an MIT open-source app. Redistribution rights, license compatibility, and F-Droid/open-source distribution are unaddressed. The plan is also not backed by any review of Cirrus terms.
attacks.evidence: "distributed as a prebuilt binary (iOS xcframework, Android AAR) under the Cirrus commercial license"

attacks.claim: GPS tracks and workout data for 90k users will go to a third-party processor with no DPA, consent or disclosure update, data residency, or retention analysis. GPS tracks are sensitive (home location). Deletion relies on a 30-day vendor admin API with no verification, and users who stay on self-hosting will be forced to migrate.
attacks.evidence: "Account deletion removes the Cirrus user record and all synced records via the Cirrus admin API within 30 days." No privacy section is present.

attacks.claim: The cost model assumes 90k MAU stays under a 100k free tier, which leaves only about 11% headroom. Growth, or 'devices' counting differently from users (multi-device users, reinstalls), could exceed the cap. Post-tier pricing is not stated, and removing the self-host fallback leaves no cost escape.
attacks.evidence: "free up to 100k monthly active devices; our 90k fits the free tier" (90k is active users, not devices)

attacks.claim: Moving data into the Cirrus store and then Cirrus Cloud is hard to reverse. There is no rollback path from Cirrus back to REST after the 30-day backup is deleted, and the 3.x restore would lose later synced data. Vendor exit, shutdown, or price change has no exit plan, and the 5.0 REST removal is a one-way door.
attacks.evidence: "the backup is deleted only after 30 days and two successful syncs"; "Legacy REST sync is removed in app 5.0"

attacks.claim: The load-bearing claims about Cirrus (record-level resumable uploads, hybrid logical clock support, free-tier terms, handling of GPS track volume) are unprototyped. The spike is only week 1 of a 5-week plan with no go/no-go gate, even though the whole plan hinges on them. The success metric of a 99.5% sync rate is measured only on beta, and the 'down 80%' target has no baseline method.
attacks.evidence: "Week 1: Cirrus integration spike"; "a dropped connection never leaves a partial workout"

attacks.claim: The 3.x downgrade restore from stride-backup-v3.db silently discards workouts recorded or synced after migration. Conflict resolution is also incomplete: last-writer-wins with device-stamped HLC is vulnerable to clock skew. 14 documented scenarios do not cover tombstone expiry (90 days) against devices offline longer, which can resurrect deleted workouts.
attacks.evidence: "Deletes are tombstones retained 90 days so an offline device cannot resurrect a deleted workout."; "3.x detects stride-backup-v3.db and restores from it"

attacks.claim: The legacy REST path is built in week 3 and only behind a flag, so self-host users get only one week of testing before the beta. The beta covers 500 volunteers with no stated self-host cohort. The plan also has no alerting for Cirrus Cloud outages or vendor SLA.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: ... legacy REST path behind custom-server flag."; "Week 4: beta ... to 500 volunteers"

attacks.claim: Self-hosting users, who chose Stride for data ownership, get an announced end of life with no migration path to Cirrus-free sync. The fix for trail-run sync could be achieved with idempotent client-generated IDs and resumable uploads on the existing REST protocol, and the plan never evaluates this option.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: alternatives considered (e.g. idempotent REST/self-hostable sync); "Current REST sync uploads whole-workout blobs"
